lines: If a tornado warning hits, do not stay in a car or a mobile home.
Sam sees dark spinning clouds above his house with 2 minutes before impact.
The roaring tornado slams into the sturdy building, shattering glass and outer walls.
Sam rushes downstairs and goes straight inside the underground basement shelter for safety.
One. Go to the basement, or an interior room on the lowest floor with no windows.
Sam secures himself in the dark basement as loud warning sirens blare outside.
Two. Put as many walls as possible between your body and the storm outside.
He retreats deeper into the corner, placing thick walls between himself and exterior doors.
Three. Cover your head and neck with your arms, a mattress or helmets.
Sam pulls a heavy mattress over his head and drops down into a crouch.
Cars and mobile homes are not safe, so hiding in this sturdy building protects him.
The entire home shakes violently while terrifying flying debris impacts the upper structure.
Heavy wind roars wildly above while the tornado passes directly over his safe position.
Sam follows every official safety rule to withstand this dangerous extreme weather disaster.
It was the perfect plan to survive the storm. There was just one problem.
An outer basement window shatters, blowing glass and roaring wind directly into his room.
part1.cliffhanger: An outer basement window shatters, blowing glass and wind into Sam's room and forcing him to quickly find an interior room with no windows.
